conventions.convention: Scalar steps satisfy h>0. Evaluation errors are absolute per-call bounds, with no independence, correlation, or relative-error assumption.
The scalar central evaluation contribution is δ/h; 2δ/h is an explicitly conservative common bound. The central balancing step optimizes that conservative bound.
Complex-step estimation uses a holomorphic extension real on a real interval; imaginary-component error contributes δ_im/h.
Directional products use m,n≥1 and Euclidean norms. Vector error bounds apply per evaluation call; random bounded errors satisfy the bounds almost surely.
Structural rows and columns are indexed from zero. Safe supports contain every actual nonzero; graph edges join columns sharing a declared row support, including structurally allowed zero entries.
Richardson extrapolation is (4D⁰_(h/2)−D⁰_h)/3; its guarantee requires one coefficient c₂ and one remainder constant M valid uniformly over 0<t≤h.
Balancing optimizes the displayed upper bounds over permitted steps (0,H], rather than actual derivative error; zero noise and zero truncation constants have separately stated cases.

load_bearing.statement: For h>0, C² regularity and |f''|≤M₂ on the forward stencil interval give |D⁺_h f(x)−f'(x)|≤M₂h/2; C³ regularity and |f'''|≤M₃ on the central stencil interval give |D⁰_h f(x)−f'(x)|≤M₃h²/6. Per-call absolute errors ≤δ add at most 2δ/h forward and δ/h central, with 2δ/h also displayed as a conservative central bound.

For h>0 with [x−h,x+h]⊂I, f∈C⁵ on a neighborhood of that interval and |f⁽⁵⁾|≤M₅ throughout it imply D⁰_h f(x)=f'(x)+f'''(x)h²/6+r_h, with |r_h|≤M₅h⁴/120. The coefficient f'''(x)/6 is the same for every admissible h at fixed x.

A safe structural row pattern satisfies J_ij=0 whenever j∉S_i. Distinct columns interfere exactly when some S_i contains both; a proper coloring assigns adjacent columns different labels, and sᶜ is the indicator vector of color c.

For a proper coloring of a safe structural row pattern, every j∈S_i with χ(j)=c satisfies J_ij=(Jsᶜ)_i; entries outside S_i are zero. Thus all entries are recovered from one compressed product per color.

For positive truncation constants and δ>0, M₂h/2+2δ/h has unique unconstrained minimizer √(4δ/M₂), and M₃h²/6+2δ/h has unique unconstrained minimizer ∛(6δ/M₃). On (0,H], each minimizer is capped at H. Zero-constant cases are stated separately.
